terms.name: Workflow
terms.means: A directed graph of steps, written as YAML and deployed to the engine. Each submission is one run of it. Every machine here is one workflow, in its workflow.yaml.

terms.name: Step (activity)
terms.means: One node of a workflow: a "- key:" entry under "activities:" in workflow.yaml, naming the worker that runs it, the activity it calls, its parameters and its outputs. These pages say step; the YAML and the engine's events say activity.

terms.name: depends_on
terms.means: A step's list of the steps it waits for. An entry with no conditions is required. An entry with conditions applies only when they hold; when they don't, the entry is not applicable rather than failed.

terms.name: Condition
terms.means: A template expression on a depends_on entry, such as {{ dial.echo.room < dial.echo.setpoint }}. Several on one entry must all hold; the engine runs the step when any entry applies.

terms.name: Skipped
terms.means: A step none of whose dependencies apply is skipped, not failed. A skip carries on to the steps that need it, unless their own conditions say otherwise.

terms.name: Loop and rounds
terms.means: A step that depends on itself, or on a step after it, runs again while its conditions hold, up to iteration_limit (100 by default). Each run of it is a round.

terms.name: Signal
terms.means: A step with wait_for_signal pauses until something outside the engine signals it through the API, or until timeout_seconds runs out; on_timeout then says whether it runs anyway, is skipped or fails.

terms.name: Delay
terms.means: A step's settings.delay holds it back for that long once its dependencies are met, before it's scheduled.

terms.name: Retry
terms.means: A failed attempt can be tried again, as the step's retry settings allow. The engine alone decides whether it does.

terms.name: Worker
terms.means: A process that asks the engine for activities and runs them. std is the built-in worker; other workers use the worker API.

terms.name: Orchestrator
terms.means: The part of the engine that reads each workflow's events and decides what runs next.

terms.name: Event
terms.means: Every change in a run, such as ActivityScheduled or ActivityCompleted, is an event in the workflow's log in PostgreSQL. The orchestrator works from that log, and the timing diagrams are drawn from it.

terms.name: Queue row
terms.means: An activity waiting for a worker, or claimed by one, is a row in the activity queue table.

terms.name: Claim timeout
terms.means: How long a worker's claim on an activity lasts without a heartbeat. After it, the activity goes back to the queue for another worker.

terms.name: Schematic
terms.analog: A circuit drawn as parts and wires.
terms.means: The workflow drawn the same way: each step a part, lit by what it did; each depends_on entry a wire; a diamond where the entry has conditions.

terms.name: Andon
terms.analog: On a factory floor, a board of lights showing each station's state.
terms.means: The row of machine names under the header: one lamp per machine, coloured by its worst run in the chosen results set.

terms.name: At the edge
terms.analog: Edge computing: devices in the field, where the network, the power or the operator can't be trusted.
terms.means: What this machine would be on such a device. It's the card's edge field.

terms.name: Pull the plug, twin
terms.analog: Pulling a machine's power cord mid-run, then plugging it back in.
terms.means: In plug mode each run gets a twin. Partway through the twin, the engine's tasks are stopped in-process and restarted on the same database, and the twin's outcome is compared with the run's: identical, different, hung, or missed.

terms.name: Footprint
terms.analog: The space a part takes on a circuit board.
terms.means: What a run took from the engine: its events and their stored size, queue rows, and the engine's peak connections.

terms.name: Trap
terms.analog: A trap set for one thing.
terms.means: A machine that reproduces a filed bug. Its runs report known broken until the fix lands, then fixed.

terms.name: Datasheet
terms.analog: A component's datasheet: its features, pinout, limits and measured characteristics.
terms.means: The machine's interface and behaviour, read from its workflow.yaml and from every run in every results set.

terms.name: Pinout
terms.analog: Which pin of a chip does what.
terms.means: Inputs are the INPUT fields and secrets the workflow reads, and each signal it waits for, as an interrupt pin. Outputs are the outputs of the steps nothing depends on.

terms.name: Absolute maximum ratings
terms.analog: The limits a part must not be driven past.
terms.means: The limits the workflow sets: iteration_limit, timeout_seconds, retries and budget. Past one, the engine ends the loop, ends the wait, stops retrying or stops on the budget.

terms.name: Characteristics
terms.analog: A datasheet's min, typical and max measurements.
terms.means: Each run's time and each step's rounds, as min, typical and max over every run in every results set.

terms.name: Ladder logic
terms.analog: A PLC program drawn as rungs between two power rails: power reaches a rung's coil when its contacts close.
terms.means: One rung per step, drawn from workflow.yaml by the engine's dependency rules. Its depends_on entries are the contacts; the coil is the step.

terms.name: Contact
terms.means: One depends_on entry, closed once its step has completed (or, with conditions, finished). Contacts in series must all close: a fan-in is an AND.

terms.name: Coil
terms.analog: The relay or output a rung drives.
terms.means: The step itself. Energized, it's scheduled to run. Click one to see its activity in workflow.yaml.

terms.name: Seal-in
terms.analog: A contact that keeps a rung energized once it has run.
terms.means: A loop's back-edge: the depends_on entry that closes the loop, so the step runs again while its conditions hold.

terms.name: Timer (TON) and counter (CTU)
terms.analog: A PLC's on-delay timer and up-counter.
terms.means: TON is settings.delay, or a signal wait's timeout_seconds. CTU counts a loop step's rounds and opens at iteration_limit.

terms.name: Interrupt
terms.analog: A line that tells a processor something outside needs it now.
terms.means: A signal: the interrupt contact closes when the step's signal arrives, and the timing diagrams' /INT line dips for each one taken.

terms.name: Timing diagram
terms.analog: A logic analyzer's capture: one channel per signal over time.
terms.means: One channel per step, drawn from the run's events: high while scheduled or running, dashed at mid-level while waiting for a signal, low when idle.

terms.name: Title block
terms.analog: The box on an engineering drawing that names it, its revision, and who drew and checked it.
terms.means: The drawing number stays with the machine. Rev is the tree and commit of the results set shown, and that results set is the checker.
